reason: The binomial bias identity, strictness, error and tail bounds, one-stratum consistency, and one-sided unbiasedness agree with (b)-(d). No likelihood, constrained parameter domain, maximizer, uniqueness, or identification of max(r1-r0,0) as the saturated ML score is stated; (a), its interior assertion, the explicit strict-bias event probability, and a joint fixed-strata statement are absent. Finite binomial denominators are positive and counts stay in range.

The stated six-atom law is exactly the constant-score counterexample and the type-7 cutoff refutes the printed c->0 reason, while leaving the no-impact conclusion intact. The inverse empirical CDF convention and the separate power-level formula are not stated. FIV bundles all IV conditions, but the numerical 3/4 and 1/4 arm means are not separately exported. No stochastic fitted-score claim is substituted for the oracle-score claim.

The type-7 count and fraction bounds, lower bound, bounded weighted-mean estimate, and finite-covariate probability limits match the corrected assertions. The sharper count<=floor(h) step is not exported, and the half-score component is uniqueness conditional on being a quantile, without existence. The sample-limit block adds RatiosEventuallyDefined for both original and Winsorized ratios: almost surely each is defined at all sufficiently large n. This is an additional hypothesis beyond canonical uniform consistency in probability, not a consequence assumed silently. Conditional-mean versions and measurability are explicit.

The corrected Bernoulli product, one-sided restriction, likelihood identity and exact equivalence of maximizers match (a)-(b), for an arbitrary parameterized probability array. Only the two specified interior numerical checks of the printed additive factor are retained from (c); its general formulas and universal lower bound of one are absent. No optimizer existence or likelihood equality is assumed as a hypothesis.

The nested conditional probabilities, no-defier type partition, range with both nested parameters interior, and positive-score cancellation match the corrected content. The first probability block additionally assumes positive AC mass, including when asserting the receipt formula. The misconditioning claim (iii) is replaced by an explicit one-profile four-atom example. The full weighted-ITT integral and a separate corrected estimator-display equality are absent; cancellation is scalar algebra only.

The binary thresholds, type partition, monotone potential receipts, failure/nonuniqueness of the printed self-referential equation, and outcome algebra are correct for arbitrary real indices. Normal/logistic laws, independent noise draws and parameters, and balanced assignment in the corrected simulation recipe are absent. The baseline and nonlinear formulas are merely unused definitions, not probabilistic assertions.

Read as an audit of the false printed ordering, the theorem negates precisely the universal profilewise implication from typical mean ignorability to latent mean ignorability and supplies the required reverse-direction witness. Positive profile mass and positive complier score keep the counterexample conditional means meaningful. The six-atom baseline-selection example has constant effects but unequal received-treatment conditional potential-outcome means. Independent finite-law checks confirm both directions can be separated; the theorem does not merely show failure of an unrelated independence assertion.

The two negative clauses refute the printed three-conclusion sufficiency implications, respectively under marginal independence of the complier indicator and conditional independence of the full type. Negating a conjunction is the appropriate refutation of those conjunctions; it does not assert that all their components fail. The constant-effect part adds measurable score/effect versions and a uniform positive score lower bound, and limits eventwise profile identities to positive-mass, positive-score profiles. It gives population identities, with no sample limits. The marginal clause does not separately refute the full-type marginal-independence alternative.

An admissible saturated two-sided Bernoulli model with 16 observations and positive weights gives a global inside-log minimizer which is not a weighted-likelihood minimizer. This is a genuine counterexample to the exact observation-weight fitting contract attributed to the package criterion. All logs have positive arguments; the article recommendation and actual numerical solver outputs are not what is refuted. Binary covariates allow the interior cell probabilities to be represented by the nested probit model.

The integrable binary-potential-outcome setting and the IV assumptions yield both ITT identities and the exact LATE/Wald ratio. Nonempty sample arms and the nonzero first stage are precisely the definedness conditions of the sample statement. The centered IV coefficient equality and all three gender-example values, including the rounding interval, match the canonical formal claim. The unused covariate type can be instantiated by Unit, so its inclusion does not exclude any law of the no-covariate claim.

The population score-weighted identities and probability limit have the correct estimand and observable weights. The sample theorem chooses explicit sufficient regularity: iid full joint draws, integrable potentials, measurable conditional-mean versions, estimates in (0,1], maximum observed score error converging in probability, second-countable Borel covariates, and supportwise A1/overlap. It additionally assumes almost sure eventual definedness of the sample ratios, stronger than definedness with probability tending to one. The population block uses uniform almost sure overlap too. Thus it does not prove consistency from pointwise Assumption 2 alone.

The Bayes density identity, LATE integral and finite-sample constant-score cancellation are faithful. The density statement does not assume overlap and remains meaningful through the complier-weighted law. The sample-limit block adds the same explicit regularity and almost sure eventual ratio-definedness as T26, along with supportwise overlap; it targets the population covariate average of complier effects without assuming A1. Constant-score cancellation is explicitly limited to defined sample ratios.
